subtopic: PyTorch Profiler vs Nsight Systems: choosing the right tool
learningObjective: Compare PyTorch Profiler with Nsight Systems/Compute and choose the appropriate tool for a given debugging task.

softwareContext.framework: PyTorch Profiler / Nsight Systems / Nsight Compute

stem: Which statements about the split between PyTorch Profiler, Nsight Systems, and Nsight Compute are correct? (Select all that apply.)

options.text: Nsight Compute samples inside a single kernel (SM utilization, warp stall reasons, memory throughput, cache hit rate); it is the right tool for optimizing a specific kernel that you have already identified as the bottleneck via Nsight Systems or PyTorch Profiler.
All three tools show the same information — kernel timeline, SM utilization, and warp stall reasons — with different UIs; picking one is a matter of preference and not of debugging need.

PyTorch Profiler is the appropriate tool when you need op-level attribution (which aten op or Python line launched which kernel) and a timeline view that unifies CPU-side dispatcher work, autograd events, and CUDA kernel launches.

Nsight Systems is oriented at system-level tracing (CPU, GPU, CUDA API, NVTX, cuDNN library calls, stream utilization); it is the right tool for diagnosing CPU launch gaps, PCIe bottlenecks, and cross-stream concurrency issues.

explanation: Correct: A, C, D.  A: Correct: per-kernel deep dive is Nsight Compute's scope. B: Wrong: tools do not fully overlap. C: Correct: op-level attribution is PyTorch Profiler's strength. D: Correct: system tracing is Nsight Systems's scope.

optionExplanations.A: Correct: per-kernel deep dive is Nsight Compute's scope.
optionExplanations.B: Wrong: tools do not fully overlap.
optionExplanations.C: Correct: op-level attribution is PyTorch Profiler's strength.
optionExplanations.D: Correct: system tracing is Nsight Systems's scope.

assumptions: Modern versions of all three tools as of 2024-2025.
nonImplications: Does not imply one tool is 'best'; the workflow typically composes them (system → op → kernel).
Does not imply the tools always agree numerically; slightly different measurement scopes can produce different numbers.
